subject: Benchmark deliverables catalogue + exec briefing for MAP close
messages:
From: Tara Singh <tara@apexdata.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-05-10T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: MAP deliverables for performance eval (APX-4271)

Hi Sean,

Thanks again for the demo earlier. As we put the MAP/close plan together, procurement has asked for the concrete performance artifacts we'll get before sign. Can you confirm what you'll deliver for latency/concurrency benchmarks (slides, raw CSVs, dashboards), and the timeline to get them into our exec readout?

We're particularly sensitive to TTFT (time-to-first-token) at low latencies for our interactive agents, plus 99th p95/p99 latency numbers and concurrency/QPS curves. Also, we need artifact naming/versioning so our SRE can ingest CSVs into internal dashboards.

Target close: end of May. Can your team commit to a packaging hand-off + exec readout before 5/24?

Best,
Tara
Tara Singh
Head of Platform, ApexData
[phone: +1-415-555-0148]

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Tara Singh <tara@apexdata.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-05-11T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP deliverables for performance eval (APX-4271)

Hi Tara — thanks for the clear ask. Below is the packaging plan we propose for the MAP deliverables and the timeline. TL;DR: yes — we can hand off a complete benchmark package + short exec slide deck before 5/24.

Deliverables (what you'll receive):
- Executive readout (pptx, 6 slides): summary, key metrics (p50/p95/p99, TTFT), concurrency curve, cost/QPS bullet, recommended runtime config.
- Raw exports (CSV): per-run token timelines, tail-latency samples, KV-cache hit logs. Filenames will follow: apx_<model>_bench_<date>_v#.csv
- Dashboard snapshot: read-only Grafana dashboard + permalink (includes live QPS, latency percentiles, TTFT heatmap).
- Packaging checklist (txt/md) with environment details: model version, quantization, batch sizes, sequence lengths, and hardware SKU.
- Quick reproducibility script (bash) to replay a small subset of requests to validate numbers.

Metrics we'll report explicitly:
- TTFT median/p95/p99 (ms) for cold and warm starts
- Token-level p50/p95/p99 latencies (ms) across representative prompts
- Sustained throughput (qps) at target latencies; concurrency curve up to agreed limit (we'll cap at 1k concurrent for the MAP run unless you ask otherwise)
- Cost per 1M tokens estimate (dedicated v. hosted)

Timeline (target):
- 05/12: baseline runs complete and first CSV export (I attached initial CSV sample).
- 05/15: full benchmark runs + dashboard snapshot.
- 05/18: internal packaging + draft exec readout shared with Marissa.
- 05/22: final package (pptx + CSVs + dashboard links) delivered to Apex and uploaded to shared Drive.
- 05/24: executive readout (30-min) with Redwood and Apex leadership.

Attachments: apx_benchmark_results_v1.csv (sample export), apx_exec_readout_outline.pptx (outline).

Questions we have for you now:
1) Do you want TTFT measured from the very first request cold start, or after a 5-request warmup? We can provide both but need to align naming.
2) Any constrained hardware SKUs we should test (e.g., single-GPU T4-equivalent only)?

If this looks good I'll lock the timeline and Marissa will own the exec slide.

Thanks,
Sean Gallagher
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: apx_benchmark_results_v1.csv (CSV)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tara Singh <tara@apexdata.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-05-12T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP deliverables for performance eval (APX-4271)

Quick packaging checklist from my side — will take point on the executive readout layout:

Packaging checklist (for final delivery):
- Slide deck (6): 1) Exec summary (key callouts) 2) Test matrix & environment 3) Latency summary (p50/p95/p99 + TTFT) 4) Concurrency/QPS curves 5) Cost implications + recommended runtime config 6) Appendix: raw CSV links + run notes.
- CSV exports: one row per request with timestamp, model, seed prompt id, first_token_delta_ms, token_delta_ms, token_index, kv_cache_hit.
- Naming convention: apx-redwood-<model>-<seq>-bench-YYYYMMDD-vN.csv
- Dashboard: snapshot + permalink; include note about time window & query used.
- Readout notes: 3 bullets per slide for execs (impact, risk, recommended next step).

Performance targets (Apex ask):
- TTFT: < 1500ms median, < 2500ms p95 for interactive prompts (cold after 1 warmup).
- Token p95: < 120ms for long-form (>512 tokens).
- Sustained QPS: show plateau and 95% latency at each concurrency point.

I'll produce the deck draft by 05/18 and will include a one-slide appendix that maps CSV fields to our dashboard panels.

Marissa Cole
Director, Product Ops — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: apx_map_delivery_checklist.md (MD)]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tara Singh <tara@apexdata.com>
Date: 2028-05-14T08:25:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP deliverables for performance eval (APX-4271)

A couple technical clarifications so the CSVs and dashboard are unambiguous:

1) Environment: we'll record hardware SKU (e.g., A100-80GB-dedicated-01), container image sha, and runtime mode (hosted/dedicated/private). Put those as header rows in every CSV.
2) Quantization: tests will include FP16 baseline + int8 quantized variant. I'll add a column `quant_variant` in CSV.
3) Warmup: we'll provide both cold-first-request metrics and a warm-run (after N=5 warmups). CSVs will include a `warmup_flag` true/false.

Also: I'll check-in with SRE to ensure the CSV schema matches their ingestion template. If they want a different timestamp format (epoch ms) we'll provide both but default to ISO + epoch column.

Karthik
Lead, Inference Engineering
